BUILD YOUR DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENT

Install from source

Check repository availability before obtaining source; no public binary package or package-manager installation is offered here.

Prerequisites Linux x64 Windows x64 macOS ARM64 Check, run and build

Prerequisites

Every source installation needs:

  • The complete LLVM/Clang/LLD 23.1.4 development SDK
  • Python 3.12+
  • CMake 3.24+
  • The platform’s C/C++ development files

A compiler-only LLVM installer is insufficient.

What the helper does

In a source checkout, the source-install helper uses the existing pinned SDK and HTTP dependency recipes, checks downloads and cached inputs, builds the compiler and language server, installs Runtime and standard-library resources, then checks the installed tools.

It does not install operating-system prerequisites or edit your shell profile.

Linux x64

Prerequisites

The userspace baseline is Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64/glibc. Install:

  • build-essential, CMake, Ninja, Python, Make and Perl
  • CA certificates and xz
  • The libffi, libedit, LibXml2, zstd, zlib and terminfo development packages

Keep the SDK for later native builds. Add the PATH export to your shell configuration for future sessions.

Platform limit

Other distributions need equivalent packages; no lower glibc floor is certified.

Complete Linux installation guide ↗

Exact prerequisites and qualification evidence: docs/install/linux.md in the checkout.

Windows x64

Prerequisites

  • Visual Studio Build Tools 2022’s x64 developer environment
  • C++ desktop tools, Windows/UCRT and DIA SDKs
  • Python 3.12+, CMake and Ninja

The source helper uses the full pinned LLVM SDK and native Schannel dependency recipe.

Native qualification still required

Earlier isolated developer-host installation passed; the new helper still needs native Windows qualification.

Complete Windows installation guide ↗

Follow docs/install/windows.md in the checkout.

macOS ARM64

Prerequisites

  • Apple Silicon with selected Xcode 26+ and its matching SDK/libc++
  • Python 3.12+, CMake, Make and Perl
Native installation result still pending

Compiler tests cover macOS ARM64, but the new source-install helper has no native macOS installation result yet.

A deployment target does not certify execution on that OS version.

Complete macOS installation guide ↗

Follow docs/install/macos.md in the checkout.

Check, run and build

After installing, voidc --help lists commands; voidc run --help explains execution and cache options.

Entry selection is automatic. A directory selects exact-case main.void; no entry flag is required.

Keep the installation together

This is source installation, not independently portable binary packaging. Keep the compiler, matching installed stdlib, Runtime archives and native manifests together.

Learn the compiler workflow and configure your editor.
